o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (döğü). In Ottoman Turkish less commonly دوكی (düğü, “rice”). Compare Turkish düğü (“the finest bulgur than remains after sifting”). Cognate with Kumyk дюгю (dügü, “rice”), Salar dügü, Turkmen tüwi (“rice”), Chagatai توکی (twky /⁠tügi⁠/, “rice”), Uyghur تۈگە (tüge, “millet”). Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *düg- (“to pound”), whence also Azerbaijani döymək (“to beat, to beat up, to knock”). The term referred to various pounded cereals, later gaining the sense "pounded rice" and, finally, "rice" in general.
Likely inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish *baqlava. Compare Gagauz baklava, dialectal Turkish paklava and paḫlava.
Borrowed from Persian ناتمام (nâtamâm). By surface analysis, na- + tamam.
